newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan VP may visit other states in Nicaragua trip.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan VP may visit other states in Nicaragua trip.

text.p: Taiwan Vice-President Lien Chan said on Sunday that when he makes a trip to Nicaragua in January he may stop by other countries to try to improve the island's diplomatic interests.
The state-run Central News Agency reported that Lien, who doubles as premier, said he would like to visit "many countries" but declined to reveal a specific itinerary.
"We are still arranging," the agency quoted Lien as saying when asked by reporters for details of his trip.
Lien plans to attend the inauguration of Nicaraguan President-elect Arnoldo Aleman on January 10.

Nicaragua is one of only 30 countries -- mostly poor states in Africa and central America -- that recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government instead of the rival communist Chinese government in Beijing.
Taiwan and China split after a civil war in 1949.
Beijing considers Taiwan a renegade province and seeks to isolate the island completely from the international arena until it can be reunified with the mainland.

Taiwan newspapers had reported that Lien decided to visit Nicaragua out of fear that Taipei's allies may be tempted to ditch Taipei for Beijing after South Africa announced in November it would make such a switch in 1997.
Pretoria had been Taiwan's biggest ally.
